title: Dhyana & Samadhi
description: Journey into the highest stages of yoga, exploring the profound states of meditative absorption where the observer and the observed become one.

sutra.meaning: When, however, that sense of effortless linkage of the attention joins continually to a particular location in the mind or emotions or outside into a higher dimension, it is the highest stage of yoga, that of samadhi. It may be a link to a greater yogi or to a divinity. This is experienced as illumination of the higher concentration force or person while the yogi feels as if devoid of his conditioned self.
Asamprajnat-Samadhi is the other kind of Samadhi which is attained by the constant practice of cessation of all mental modifications, in which the Chitta retains only the unmanifested impression.

sections.insight: This state is akin to the state just before falling asleep. The intelligence dissolves but the sense of self remains.
sections.reflectionPrompt: Am I close to stopping the modulations of the mind to some extent?
sections.practice: Intensify your practices to quiten the mind.

sutra.meaning: In Asamprajnat Samadhi the sadhak may experience bodilessness or become merged in nature leading to solitude.

sections.insight: In this samadhi the sadhak is freed from all modulations but the samskaras spring back to life the moment he comes out of this state.
sections.reflectionPrompt: Am I open to this kind of experience yet?
sections.practice: Intensify your practices to quiten the mind.

sutra.meaning: Practice must be persued with faith,confidence, energy, keenness of memory and the power to absorb to avoid spiritual complacency.

sections.insight: I need to put in my 100% to make progress
sections.reflectionPrompt: Inner growth needs sincerity and effort. Am I a willing sadhak?
sections.practice: Be 100% present in whatever you do today
sections.meditation: 5 mins total focus on breath meditate 20 min
sections.journalPrompt: Do I have trust in the path?

sutra.meaning:
Intense effort brings quick progress
Effort varies in intensity -i) feeble ii) moderate iii)steady

sections.insight:
Depth of desire determines growth.
The pace of growth depends on your effort.
sections.reflectionPrompt:
How strong is my intention?
Where am I on this scale?
sections.practice:
Act with intensity in all you do today.
Observe effort level

sutra.meaning:
The Chitta ie consciousness may be totaly focused and surrendered to God.
Ishvara is untouched by suffering and karma

sections.insight: The divine is pure and unaffected. The purpose of human life is to reach that state.
sections.meditation: 5 min awareness and surrender meditate 20 min

sutra.meaning:
Om is the expression of the divine
Repeat Om with awareness

sections.insight:
Sound connects to consciousness because it is at the source of all creation. Aum is the symbol of divinity.
Repetition deepens experience.
sections.reflectionPrompt: Can I feel the vibrations of the sounds around me?
sections.practice: Chant Om 11 times watching the vibrations it makes within
sections.shlokaFrom: ओमित्येकाक्षरं ब्रह्म व्याहरन्मामनुस्मरन् | य: प्रयाति त्यजन्देहं स याति परमां गतिम् || 8.13||
sections.wisdomFrom: One who departs from the body while remembering Me, the Supreme Personality, and chanting the syllable Om, will attain the supreme goal.

sutra.meaning: Om chanting leads inward and removes obstacles

sections.insight: Inner connection ie. when the experiencer, the experience and the experienced become one there is no inner or outer turmoil.
sections.reflectionPrompt: Am I able to go inwards when I sit in silence with eyes closed?
sections.practice: Observe your thoughts. Does that quieten them
sections.shlokaFrom:
कविं पुराणमनुशासितार मणोरणीयांसमनुस्मरेद्य: |
सर्वस्य धातारमचिन्त्यरूप मादित्यवर्णं तमस: परस्तात् || 8.9||
प्रयाणकाले मनसाचलेन भक्त्या युक्तो योगबलेन चैव |
भ्रुवोर्मध्ये प्राणमावेश्य सम्यक् स तं परं पुरुषमुपैति दिव्यम् || 8.10||
sections.wisdomFrom: God is Omniscient, the most ancient One, the Controller, subtler than the subtlest, the Support of all, and the possessor of an inconceivable divine form; He is brighter than the sun, and beyond all darkness of ignorance. One who at the time of death, with unmoving mind attained by the practice of Yog, fixes the prāṇ (life-airs) between the eyebrows, and steadily remembers the Divine Lord with great devotion, certainly attains Him.

sutra.meaning: Meditate on an object of your choice which is spiritually uplifting to you

sections.insight: Any sincere focus leads inward. This method of meditation by Patanjali in this group is seemingly the simplest but actually the hardest. Meditating on ones', self which is of course the most pleasant object to everyone, is the simplest and also the most difficult.
sections.practice: Meditate at a chosen spot focusing within.

sutra.meaning: Mastery extends from smallest to largest

sections.insight: Awareness expands limitlessly. Maharishi Patanjali has given various methods of dhyan or meditation  to master ones chitta or cosciousness and stop the desires from overtaking the mind.

sutra.meaning: When the seer the seen and the instrument of perception become one, the mind becomes clear and it reflects reality like a crystal

sections.insight:
When the mind is pure it reflects truth without distortion.This is a very refined state of consciousness called samapatti. 
Thus yoga and samadhi are but means to reach the state of samapatti.
sections.reflectionPrompt: Is my perception clear or colored?

sutra.meaning: Savitarka samapatti wherein perception words, their meaning simultaneously blend with understanding into a special knowledge. .

sections.insight: The sadhaks chitta has become clear like a mirror and there are no boundaries to understanding.

sutra.meaning: When memory is purified only truth shines Let go of past filters to see clearly.

sections.insight: Past impressions create biases and prejudices. Unless the slate is continuously cleaned the writing on top will be garbled.
sections.reflectionPrompt: Do I think too much of what has passed. Is my perception colored by past experiences.

sutra.sanskrit: एतयैव सविचारा निर्विचारा च सूक्ष्मविषया व्याख्याता
sutra.meaning: Awareness refines from subte to the subtlest when the sadhak moves from savichar samapatti to nirvichar samapatti.

sections.insight: Subtle states of awareness deepen perception when from meditating on  oneself or objects of the senses etc the sadhak withdraws to contemplate beyond space and time or cause and effect.

sutra.meaning: Nature at its subtlest is consciousness. When the two dissolve into one it is at its purest.

sections.insight: Awareness expands beyond form. There is total cessation of the modulations of the small mind and the appearance of the Cosmic Mind or mahat.

sutra.meaning: These are seed-based meditations, ie the sadhak's intellect or buddhi is still in play.

sections.insight: The six samapattis mentioned viz. savitarka, nirvitarka, savichara, nirvichara , ananda and asmita are all sabeej (or seeded in nature).

sutra.meaning: Nirvichar or non Reflection brings clarity in subtle awareness and inner joy

sections.insight: When the chitta (consciousness) and buddhi (intellect) remain non reflective inner clarity blossoms and brings calm and happiness.

sutra.meaning: Seasoned wisdom arises in the chitta (consciousness) and provides immense insight.

sections.insight: Inner wisdom is beyond logic and human intellect.

sutra.meaning: This wisdom differs from knowledge gained externally

sections.insight: Direct experience is different from learned knowledge.
sections.reflectionPrompt: Did I experience or just think?

sutra.meaning: New impressions are prevented whereas old patterns are erased.

sections.insight: Awareness replaces conditioning.

sutra.meaning: Even this new state of wisdom dissolves leading to a nirbeeja or seedless state

sections.insight: Ultimate stillness is beyond all patterns.

sutra.meaning: Subtle impressions dissolve by returning to source

sections.insight: Going inward dissolves patterns.

sutra.meaning: Meditation removes disturbances

sections.insight: Meditation clears mind patterns.
sections.shlokaFrom:
सङ्कल्पप्रभवान्कामांस्त्यक्त्वा सर्वानशेषत: |
मनसैवेन्द्रियग्रामं विनियम्य समन्तत: || 6.24||
शनै: शनैरुपरमेद्बुद्ध्या धृतिगृहीतया |
आत्मसंस्थं मन: कृत्वा न किञ्चिदपि चिन्तयेत् ||6. 25||
sections.wisdomFrom: We can meditate upon God in several ways. The Names, Forms, Leelas (Pastimes), Associates, and Abodes of God. There is no difference among all these aspects of God. Therefore, one can meditate on any one or all of them. Such meditation, where we attach our mind to the Supreme Divinity, takes our mind to the divine realm, and as a result, it purifies.
